requirement:
The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`, including an empty
result. A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_structure.inputs` has no structural obligation, and it has no implementation edges. Its clauses say only what the agent does. First, "The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`, including an empty result." This is a protocol duty: the agent must close every delivered search. It names no library, type, signature, field or interface. An implementation that closed searches through any other mechanism would behave the same way and still satisfy it. Second, "A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency." This describes an observable outcome, that a read records its own dependency. It does not say how a read must be built. The recording rules themselves belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`. That requirement is context only and has no refining declaration whose text adds structure here. No implementation root is needed, and none is missing.

behavioral: The subject has two behavioral obligations. (1) Each delivered `search_structure` result, including an empty one, is accounted for under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`. (2) A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency. The `finish_search.inputs` rules themselves are cited context, so I did not reassess them. I only checked that they are applied to structural results.

Test coverage, all in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` under `mod[tests]`:

- **Empty structural result.**
  - `fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` dispatches an empty `search_structure`. It asserts that `outstanding_searches()` lists exactly that search id until it is finished. It then finishes it with `used:[]` and asserts no dependencies.
  - `fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]` does the same. It asserts that the empty search has no dependencies, that `matches` is `[]` and `complete` is true, and that `finish_search` with `used:[]` records no dependencies.
- **Selected tag, original snapshot.** In `fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]`, the file is rewritten after delivery. Selecting the tag then yields exactly `Dependency::Node(code.rs#fn[two], original fingerprint)`. Selecting it twice gives the same result, so the original dependency is preserved on re-selection. An empty `used` list adds no dependency.
- **Excerpt with several outline nodes.** `fn[structural_excerpt_tracks_each_visible_node_in_the_delivered_snapshot]` searches for an `impl_item` that contains `fn a` and `fn b`. The file is rewritten after delivery. It asserts that finishing records the dependencies for `impl[S]`, `impl[S]/fn[a]` and `impl[S]/fn[b]`, each with the original fingerprint. It also asserts that an invalid call (`unknown` tag) errors and that re-finishing still returns the same dependencies, so recorded inputs stay intact.
- **Redaction.** `fn[search_excerpts_redact_credentials_before_serialization_and_paging]` checks that a selected structural tag records the fingerprint of the original `fn[chosen]` snapshot.
- **Separate tracked read.** `fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]` calls `read_node` on a structural match. It asserts that this records its own `Dependency::Node` with a content fingerprint. It also asserts that the search dispatch and the empty finish record no dependencies, and that `domain.reads == 1`.

A non-empty structural search has no explicit assertion that it appears in `outstanding_searches` before it is finished. This is not a gap. The empty structural case asserts the outstanding tracking. Finishing a non-empty result by `search_id` only succeeds if that search was registered. The mechanism has no per-result branching that the text distinguishes.

I found no obligation without a test and no marking gap.

text: The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under
result. A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency.
For each selected tag, the harness records the node identity and fingerprint
from the snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. If the excerpt also shows source owned by other outline nodes, record those nodes’ read fingerprints as well. Selecting a tag again
preserves the original dependency. Earlier selections survive later calls.
An empty `used` list adds no dependency. Unselected excerpts and the match set
add none either. An invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact.
